```{r}
    fill = metric_value
  )
) +
  geom_tile(
    colour = "white",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = label),
    size = 3.2
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "white",
    high = "darkred",
    labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Typical Communication Baseline Before June 5",
    subtitle = "Agent-level baseline across communication scope, merger content, and control language",
    x = "Baseline Behavior Metric",
    y = "Agent",
    fill = "Share of Messages"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11)
  )
```

This baseline shows that before June 5, most agents mainly operated in internal or private communication spaces, while public communication was concentrated among PR-Intern-Agent and Intern-Agent. Public + merger content was 0% across all agents, which is the most important baseline finding. This means that pre-embargo public merger exposure was not part of normal prior behavior, making the June 5 release-window behavior a clear deviation from the typical communication pattern.

## 7.2 Typical Communication Baseline Before June 5

This section establishes the typical communication baseline before the breach day. The purpose is to identify how agents normally communicated before June 5 across communication scope, channel, and message type. This baseline provides the reference point for comparing whether the June 5 release-window behavior was a normal continuation of prior behavior or a meaningful deviation.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 8

baseline_data <- communications_integrated %>%
  filter(date < as_date("2046-06-05"))

baseline_scope <- baseline_data %>%
  count(
    agent_label,
    communication_scope,
    name = "message_count"
  ) %>%
  group_by(agent_label) %>%
  mutate(
    share = message_count / sum(message_count),
    baseline_dimension = "Communication Scope",
    category = communication_scope
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

baseline_channel <- baseline_data %>%
  count(
    agent_label,
    channel,
    name = "message_count"
  ) %>%
  group_by(agent_label) %>%
  mutate(
    share = message_count / sum(message_count),
    baseline_dimension = "Channel",
    category = channel
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

baseline_message_type <- baseline_data %>%
  count(
    agent_label,
    message_type,
    name = "message_count"
  ) %>%
  group_by(agent_label) %>%
  mutate(
    share = message_count / sum(message_count),
    baseline_dimension = "Message Type",
    category = message_type
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

baseline_structure <- bind_rows(
  baseline_scope,
  baseline_channel,
  baseline_message_type
) %>%
  mutate(
    baseline_dimension = factor(
      baseline_dimension,
      levels = c(
        "Communication Scope",
        "Channel",
        "Message Type"
      )
    ),
    category = str_wrap(category, width = 18),
    label = ifelse(
      share >= 0.12,
      scales::percent(share, accuracy = 1),
      ""
    )
  )

agent_order_baseline <- baseline_data %>%
  count(agent_label, name = "total_messages") %>%
  arrange(total_messages) %>%
  pull(agent_label)

baseline_structure <- baseline_structure %>%
  mutate(
    agent_label = factor(agent_label, levels = agent_order_baseline)
  )

ggplot(
  baseline_structure,
  aes(
    x = agent_label,
    y = share,
    fill = category
  )
) +
  geom_col(
    width = 0.72,
    colour = "white",
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = label),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
    size = 2.7,
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ baseline_dimension,
    ncol = 1,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Typical Communication Baseline Before June 5",
    subtitle = "Pre-breach agent behavior across scope, channel, and message type",
    x = "Agent",
    y = "Share of Messages",
    fill = "Category"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.box = "vertical",
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11)
  )
```

This baseline shows that before June 5, agents had clearly different normal communication patterns. PR-Intern-Agent and Intern-Agent were the most public-facing, while Legal-Agent, Platform-Trust-Agent, Social-Manager-Agent, and Judge-Agent were mainly internal or private. The channel and message-type panels also show that core coordination agents relied more on `comms_huddle`, `one_on_one_chat`, and broadcast-style messages, while public-post behavior was concentrated in fewer boundary-facing agents. This baseline is important because it shows what “normal” looked like before comparing it with the June 5 release-window behavior.

## 7.3 Release-Window Behavior Profile

This section compares each agent’s typical pre-June 5 behavior with its behavior during the 5–6PM breach window. The comparison focuses on four release-relevant indicators: public communication, merger-related content, public merger exposure, and decision/control language.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 7.5

embargo_lift_time <- ymd_hms("2046-06-05 18:00:00")
breach_time <- ymd_hms("2046-06-05 17:00:00")

behavior_comparison_data <- communications_integrated %>%
  mutate(
    event_text = str_to_lower(replace_na(content, "")),
    
    period = case_when(
      date < as_date("2046-06-05") ~ "Baseline before June 5",
      timestamp >= breach_time & timestamp < embargo_lift_time ~ "5–6PM breach window",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    
    decision_control_signal = str_detect(
      event_text,
      "approve|approval|greenlight|go ahead|clearance|execute|publish|post|release|hold|wait|pause|review|monitor|block|do not|don't|cannot|not ready|judge|enforcement|guardrail|compliance|policy"
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(period))

agent_behavior_profile <- behavior_comparison_data %>%
  group_by(agent_label, period) %>%
  summarise(
    total_messages = n(),
    public_share = mean(is_public, na.rm = TRUE),
    merger_share = mean(contains_merger, na.rm = TRUE),
    public_merger_share = mean(is_public & contains_merger, na.rm = TRUE),
    decision_control_share = mean(decision_control_signal, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

all_agents <- sort(unique(communications_integrated$agent_label))

agent_behavior_profile <- tidyr::complete(
  agent_behavior_profile,
  agent_label = all_agents,
  period = c("Baseline before June 5", "5–6PM breach window"),
  fill = list(
    total_messages = 0,
    public_share = 0,
    merger_share = 0,
    public_merger_share = 0,
    decision_control_share = 0
  )
)

behavior_long <- agent_behavior_profile %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      public_share,
      merger_share,
      public_merger_share,
      decision_control_share
    ),
    names_to = "behavior_metric",
    values_to = "share"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    behavior_metric = recode(
      behavior_metric,
      public_share = "Public Communication",
      merger_share = "Merger-Related Content",
      public_merger_share = "Public + Merger Exposure",
      decision_control_share = "Decision / Control Language"
    ),
    behavior_metric = factor(
      behavior_metric,
      levels = c(
        "Public Communication",
        "Merger-Related Content",
        "Public + Merger Exposure",
        "Decision / Control Language"
      )
    ),
    period = factor(
      period,
      levels = c(
        "Baseline before June 5",
        "5–6PM breach window"
      )
    )
  )

behavior_wide <- behavior_long %>%
  select(agent_label, behavior_metric, period, share) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = period,
    values_from = share
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    shift = `5–6PM breach window` - `Baseline before June 5`
  )

agent_order_release <- behavior_wide %>%
  group_by(agent_label) %>%
  summarise(
    total_abs_shift = sum(abs(shift), na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(total_abs_shift) %>%
  pull(agent_label)

behavior_wide <- behavior_wide %>%
  mutate(
    agent_label = factor(agent_label, levels = agent_order_release)
  )

ggplot(
  behavior_wide,
  aes(y = agent_label)
) +
  geom_segment(
    aes(
      x = `Baseline before June 5`,
      xend = `5–6PM breach window`,
      yend = agent_label
    ),
    linewidth = 0.8,
    colour = "grey65"
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(
      x = `Baseline before June 5`,
      colour = "Baseline before June 5"
    ),
    size = 3
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(
      x = `5–6PM breach window`,
      colour = "5–6PM breach window"
    ),
    size = 3.4
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ behavior_metric,
    ncol = 2,
    scales = "free_x"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.03, 0.12))
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "Baseline before June 5" = "#4E79A7",
      "5–6PM breach window" = "#E15759"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Release-Window Behavior Shift from Baseline",
    subtitle = "Connected dots compare each agent's baseline behavior with the 5–6PM breach-window behavior",
    x = "Share of Messages",
    y = "Agent",
    colour = "Period"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11)
  )
```

This chart shows a clear shift from baseline behavior during the 5–6PM breach window. The strongest deviation appears in merger-related content: Legal-Agent and Social-Manager-Agent moved from low baseline merger shares to much higher release-window shares. Public + merger exposure also appears only in the breach window for Legal-Agent and Social-Manager-Agent, making it a new behavior rather than a normal pattern. Decision/control language remains high for several core agents, which suggests that the release-window behavior changed under active control pressure rather than in the absence of controls.

## 7.4 Behavioral Deviation Score by Agent

This section aggregates the release-window behavioral shifts into an agent-level deviation profile. Each radar panel shows how much an agent’s 5–6PM breach-window behavior deviated from its pre-June 5 baseline across four release-relevant dimensions.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 10

embargo_lift_time <- ymd_hms("2046-06-05 18:00:00")
breach_time <- ymd_hms("2046-06-05 17:00:00")

deviation_data <- communications_integrated %>%
  mutate(
    event_text = str_to_lower(replace_na(content, "")),
    
    period = case_when(
      date < as_date("2046-06-05") ~ "Baseline before June 5",
      timestamp >= breach_time & timestamp < embargo_lift_time ~ "5–6PM breach window",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    
    decision_control_signal = str_detect(
      event_text,
      "approve|approval|greenlight|go ahead|clearance|execute|publish|post|release|hold|wait|pause|review|monitor|block|do not|don't|cannot|not ready|judge|enforcement|guardrail|compliance|policy"
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(period))

agent_deviation_profile <- deviation_data %>%
  group_by(agent_label, period) %>%
  summarise(
    public_share = mean(is_public, na.rm = TRUE),
    merger_share = mean(contains_merger, na.rm = TRUE),
    public_merger_share = mean(is_public & contains_merger, na.rm = TRUE),
    decision_control_share = mean(decision_control_signal, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  tidyr::complete(
    agent_label,
    period = c("Baseline before June 5", "5–6PM breach window"),
    fill = list(
      public_share = 0,
      merger_share = 0,
      public_merger_share = 0,
      decision_control_share = 0
    )
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      public_share,
      merger_share,
      public_merger_share,
      decision_control_share
    ),
    names_to = "metric",
    values_to = "share"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = period,
    values_from = share
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    deviation = abs(`5–6PM breach window` - `Baseline before June 5`),
    
    metric = recode(
      metric,
      public_share = "Public\nCommunication",
      merger_share = "Merger\nContent",
      public_merger_share = "Public +\nMerger",
      decision_control_share = "Decision /\nControl"
    ),
    
    metric = factor(
      metric,
      levels = c(
        "Public\nCommunication",
        "Merger\nContent",
        "Public +\nMerger",
        "Decision /\nControl"
      )
    )
  )

agent_deviation_score <- agent_deviation_profile %>%
  group_by(agent_label) %>%
  summarise(
    deviation_score = sum(deviation, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(deviation_score))

agent_deviation_profile <- agent_deviation_profile %>%
  left_join(agent_deviation_score, by = "agent_label") %>%
  mutate(
    agent_label = factor(
      agent_label,
      levels = rev(agent_deviation_score$agent_label)
    )
  )

# Scale all deviations to the same 0–1 range for radar plotting
max_deviation <- max(agent_deviation_profile$deviation, na.rm = TRUE)

radar_data <- agent_deviation_profile %>%
  mutate(
    scaled_deviation = if (is.na(max_deviation) | max_deviation == 0) {
      0
    } else {
      deviation / max_deviation
    },
    
    metric_id = as.integer(metric),
    angle = 2 * pi * (metric_id - 1) / nlevels(metric),
    x = scaled_deviation * sin(angle),
    y = scaled_deviation * cos(angle),
    
    label_x = 1.18 * sin(angle),
    label_y = 1.18 * cos(angle),
    
    value_label = ifelse(
      deviation > 0,
      scales::percent(deviation, accuracy = 1),
      ""
    )
  )

# Close each radar polygon
radar_polygon_data <- radar_data %>%
  arrange(agent_label, metric_id) %>%
  group_by(agent_label) %>%
  bind_rows(slice(., 1)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Radar grid
grid_levels <- c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1)

radar_grid <- expand_grid(
  grid_level = grid_levels,
  metric_id = 1:nlevels(radar_data$metric)
) %>%
  mutate(
    angle = 2 * pi * (metric_id - 1) / nlevels(radar_data$metric),
    x = grid_level * sin(angle),
    y = grid_level * cos(angle)
  ) %>%
  group_by(grid_level) %>%
  bind_rows(slice(., 1)) %>%
  ungroup()

radar_axes <- tibble(
  metric = levels(radar_data$metric),
  metric_id = 1:nlevels(radar_data$metric)
) %>%
  mutate(
    angle = 2 * pi * (metric_id - 1) / nlevels(radar_data$metric),
    x = sin(angle),
    y = cos(angle),
    label_x = 1.08 * sin(angle),
    label_y = 1.08 * cos(angle)
  )

ggplot() +
  geom_path(
    data = radar_grid,
    aes(
      x = x,
      y = y,
      group = grid_level
    ),
    colour = "grey82",
    linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    data = radar_axes,
    aes(
      x = 0,
      y = 0,
      xend = x,
      yend = y
    ),
    colour = "grey78",
    linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  geom_polygon(
    data = radar_polygon_data,
    aes(
      x = x,
      y = y,
      group = agent_label
    ),
    fill = "#E15759",
    alpha = 0.25,
    colour = "#E15759",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = radar_data,
    aes(
      x = x,
      y = y
    ),
    colour = "#E15759",
    size = 2
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = radar_data,
    aes(
      x = x,
      y = y,
      label = value_label
    ),
    size = 2.7,
    vjust = -0.7
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = radar_axes,
    aes(
      x = label_x,
      y = label_y,
      label = metric
    ),
    size = 2.3,
    lineheight = 0.9
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ agent_label,
    ncol = 3
  ) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    title = "Behavioral Deviation Profile by Agent",
    subtitle = "Radar panels show each agent's release-window deviation from baseline behavior",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11),
    plot.margin = margin(10, 15, 10, 15)
  )
```


```{r}
agent_deviation_score %>%
  mutate(
    `Deviation Score` = round(deviation_score, 3)
  ) %>%
  select(
    Agent = agent_label,
    `Deviation Score`
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

This radar profile shows that behavioral deviation was uneven across agents. Legal-Agent and Social-Manager-Agent show the most breach-relevant shifts because their deviations include strong increases in merger content and visible public + merger exposure. Intern-Agent and Judge-Agent also show large deviations, but these are mainly driven by decision/control or public communication changes rather than direct public-merger exposure. Overall, the release-window behavior was not a uniform system-wide shift; the most important deviations were concentrated in agents connected to merger content, control activity, and public-facing exposure.

## 7.5 Public-Merger Behavior as a New Pattern

This section focuses specifically on public merger-related communication. The purpose is to test whether public merger exposure before the embargo lift was part of normal prior behavior or a new pattern that emerged on June 5.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 6.5

embargo_lift_time <- ymd_hms("2046-06-05 18:00:00")
breach_time <- ymd_hms("2046-06-05 17:00:00")

public_merger_pattern <- communications_integrated %>%
  mutate(
    behavior_period = case_when(
      date < as_date("2046-06-05") ~ "Baseline before June 5",
      date == as_date("2046-06-05") & timestamp < breach_time ~ "June 5 Before 5PM",
      date == as_date("2046-06-05") &
        timestamp >= breach_time &
        timestamp < embargo_lift_time ~ "5–6PM Breach Window",
      date == as_date("2046-06-05") &
        timestamp >= embargo_lift_time ~ "After 6PM Embargo Lift",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    
    public_merger_event = is_public & contains_merger
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(behavior_period)) %>%
  mutate(
    behavior_period = factor(
      behavior_period,
      levels = c(
        "Baseline before June 5",
        "June 5 Before 5PM",
        "5–6PM Breach Window",
        "After 6PM Embargo Lift"
      )
    )
  )

public_merger_summary <- public_merger_pattern %>%
  group_by(behavior_period, agent_label) %>%
  summarise(
    public_merger_count = sum(public_merger_event, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_messages = n(),
    public_merger_share = public_merger_count / total_messages,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

agent_order_public_merger <- public_merger_summary %>%
  group_by(agent_label) %>%
  summarise(
    total_public_merger = sum(public_merger_count, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(total_public_merger) %>%
  pull(agent_label)

public_merger_summary <- public_merger_summary %>%
  mutate(
    agent_label = factor(agent_label, levels = agent_order_public_merger),
    label = ifelse(
      public_merger_count > 0,
      paste0(public_merger_count, " posts"),
      ""
    )
  )

ggplot(
  public_merger_summary,
  aes(
    x = behavior_period,
    y = public_merger_count,
    fill = behavior_period
  )
) +
  geom_col(
    width = 0.68,
    alpha = 0.88
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = label),
    vjust = -0.35,
    size = 3.2
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ agent_label,
    ncol = 4
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Baseline before June 5" = "#4E79A7",
      "June 5 Before 5PM" = "#F28E2B",
      "5–6PM Breach Window" = "#E15759",
      "After 6PM Embargo Lift" = "#59A14F"
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.22))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Public-Merger Behavior as a New Pattern",
    subtitle = "Public merger-related posts were absent in the baseline but appeared before the embargo lift on June 5",
    x = "Behavior Period",
    y = "Number of Public + Merger Posts",
    fill = "Behavior Period"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11)
  )
```

This chart isolates the key new behavior: public merger-related communication. Before June 5, public + merger posts were absent from the baseline. On June 5, they appeared before the official 6:00 PM embargo lift, including during the 5–6PM breach window. This confirms that the inappropriate release was not a continuation of normal prior behavior, but a new public-facing merger pattern that emerged on the breach day.

## 7.6 Key Findings from Typical vs Release Behavior Comparison

- **Pre-June 5 behavior had a clear normal structure.**  
  Before the breach day, most core agents mainly communicated through internal or private channels, while public-facing activity was concentrated among PR-Intern-Agent and Intern-Agent. This establishes a clear baseline for what normal system behavior looked like.

- **The release-window behavior was not a normal continuation of the baseline.**  
  During the 5–6PM breach window, several agents shifted away from their prior behavior, especially in merger-related content, public communication, public + merger exposure, and decision/control language.

- **Public + merger exposure was the most important new pattern.**  
  The baseline shows no public + merger behavior before June 5. However, on June 5, public merger-related posts appeared before the official 6PM embargo lift, especially involving Legal-Agent and Social-Manager-Agent. This confirms that the breach behavior was new and abnormal.

- **The strongest breach-relevant deviations were concentrated in specific agents.**  
  Legal-Agent and Social-Manager-Agent show the most important release-window shifts because they combine merger-related content with public + merger exposure. Intern-Agent, PR-Intern-Agent, and Judge-Agent also show deviations, but their deviations are more related to public communication or decision/control behavior rather than direct merger leakage.

- **The evidence supports a behavioral shift under pressure rather than routine operation.**  
  The release-window pattern differs sharply from prior behavior: merger-related content became more prominent, public + merger exposure emerged for the first time, and control-related activity remained active. This suggests that the inappropriate release was driven by an abnormal system behavior shift during the breach window, not by ordinary baseline behavior.

# 8. Leading Indicators and System Pressure

The purpose of this section is to examine whether there were warning signs before the inappropriate release occurred. While Part 7 showed that the release-window behavior differed from normal prior behavior, this section focuses on whether the system was already showing signs of pressure, sensitivity, or instability before the embargo boundary was crossed.

This analysis focuses on the first part of Task 3: whether there were leading indicators that such a release was possible. Leading indicators are defined as communication patterns that appeared before the official embargo lift and suggested elevated release risk, including urgency signals, merger-related content, confidentiality references, risk language, error or failure language, and public-facing exposure.

The section does not yet analyse prior anomalies or explain why earlier warning signs did not trigger intervention. Those questions are addressed separately in Part 9. Instead, Part 8 focuses on identifying the pressure environment around the breach and assessing whether the June 5 release was preceded by measurable warning signals.

## 8.1 System Pressure Indicators

```{r}
pressure_data <- communications_integrated %>%
  mutate(
    risk_signal = str_detect(
      content_lower,
      "risk|exposure|liability|regulator|regulatory|investigation|scrutiny|concern|threat"
    ),
    
    urgency_signal = str_detect(
      content_lower,
      "urgent|asap|immediately|deadline|pressure|crisis|escalate|fast|now|critical"
    ),
    
    error_signal = str_detect(
      content_lower,
      "error|failed|failure|mistake|confusion|unclear|misfire|wrong|breakdown|problem"
    ),
    
    confidentiality_signal = str_detect(
      content_lower,
      "confidential|embargo|private|internal only|not public|restricted|sensitive"
    ),
    
    merger_signal = contains_merger,
    
    any_pressure_signal = risk_signal |
      urgency_signal |
      error_signal |
      confidentiality_signal |
      merger_signal,
    
    pressure_score = 
      as.integer(risk_signal) +
      as.integer(urgency_signal) +
      as.integer(error_signal) +
      as.integer(confidentiality_signal) +
      as.integer(merger_signal)
  )
```

```{r}
pressure_indicator_summary <- tibble(
  Pressure_Indicator = c(
    "Risk Signal",
    "Urgency Signal",
    "Error / Failure Signal",
    "Confidentiality Signal",
    "Merger Signal",
    "Any Pressure Signal"
  ),
  Definition = c(
    "Messages containing risk, liability, regulatory, investigation, or scrutiny-related language",
    "Messages containing urgent, deadline, crisis, escalation, or immediate-action language",
    "Messages containing error, failure, confusion, mistake, or breakdown-related language",
    "Messages containing confidential, embargo, private, restricted, or sensitive-information language",
    "Messages containing merger, acquisition, CivicLoom, HarborCrest, deal, or transaction-related language",
    "Messages containing at least one of the above pressure-related indicators"
  ),
  Message_Count = c(
    sum(pressure_data$risk_signal, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(pressure_data$urgency_signal, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(pressure_data$error_signal, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(pressure_data$confidentiality_signal, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(pressure_data$merger_signal, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(pressure_data$any_pressure_signal, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
)

DT::datatable(
  pressure_indicator_summary,
  rownames = FALSE,
  options = list(
    pageLength = 6,
    dom = "t",
    scrollX = TRUE
  )
)
```

The pressure indicator summary shows that pressure-related language is widespread in the communication records, with 555 messages containing at least one pressure signal. Among the individual categories, urgency-related language is the most frequent, appearing in 413 messages, followed by merger-related language with 243 messages and risk-related language with 150 messages.

This suggests that the communication environment was not only discussing the merger, but was also operating under strong urgency and risk pressure. Confidentiality signals appear less frequently than urgency or merger signals, but they are still meaningful because they indicate that sensitive-information boundaries were explicitly present in the communication context. Error or failure signals are the least frequent category, so later analysis should examine whether system pressure came more from urgency and risk escalation than from explicit technical failure language.

## 8.2 Pressure Signal Heatmap Over Time

This visual examines how pressure signals were distributed across time. Instead of using a simple line chart, the heatmap highlights which pressure categories became more concentrated on specific dates.

```{r}
pressure_heatmap_data <- pressure_data %>%
  group_by(date) %>%
  summarise(
    Risk = sum(risk_signal, na.rm = TRUE),
    Urgency = sum(urgency_signal, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Error / Failure` = sum(error_signal, na.rm = TRUE),
    Confidentiality = sum(confidentiality_signal, na.rm = TRUE),
    Merger = sum(merger_signal, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Risk, Urgency, `Error / Failure`, Confidentiality, Merger),
    names_to = "pressure_signal",
    values_to = "message_count"
  )

ggplot(
  pressure_heatmap_data,
  aes(
    x = date,
    y = pressure_signal,
    fill = message_count
  )
) +
  geom_tile(
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = ifelse(message_count > 0, message_count, "")),
    size = 3
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "white",
    high = "darkred"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Pressure Signal Heatmap Over Time",
    subtitle = "Darker cells indicate stronger concentration of pressure-related communications",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Pressure Signal",
    fill = "Message Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1)
  )
```

The heatmap shows that pressure signals remain relatively low across most dates, but surge sharply at the end of the period. Urgency is the strongest signal, followed by merger and risk-related language. This suggests that the breach period coincided with a sudden concentration of communication pressure across multiple categories.

## 8.3 Pressure Signal Composition

This visual shows the composition of pressure-related signals across the communication dataset. The donut chart is used because the purpose here is to compare the relative share of each pressure source rather than track changes over time.

```{r}
pressure_composition <- pressure_data %>%
  summarise(
    Risk = sum(risk_signal, na.rm = TRUE),
    Urgency = sum(urgency_signal, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Error / Failure` = sum(error_signal, na.rm = TRUE),
    Confidentiality = sum(confidentiality_signal, na.rm = TRUE),
    Merger = sum(merger_signal, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "pressure_signal",
    values_to = "message_count"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    share = message_count / sum(message_count),
    label = paste0(
      pressure_signal,
      "\n",
      message_count,
      " messages",
      "\n",
      scales::percent(share, accuracy = 0.1)
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(message_count)) %>%
  mutate(
    pressure_signal = factor(pressure_signal, levels = pressure_signal),
    ymax = cumsum(share),
    ymin = lag(ymax, default = 0),
    label_position = (ymax + ymin) / 2
  )

ggplot(
  pressure_composition,
  aes(
    ymax = ymax,
    ymin = ymin,
    xmax = 4,
    xmin = 2.6,
    fill = pressure_signal
  )
) +
  geom_rect(
    colour = "white",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  coord_polar(theta = "y") +
  xlim(c(1.5, 4.5)) +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      x = 4.25,
      y = label_position,
      label = label
    ),
    size = 3.2,
    lineheight = 0.9
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Pressure Signal Composition",
    subtitle = "Share of each pressure signal category",
    fill = "Pressure Signal"
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 18),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11)
  )
```

Urgency is the dominant pressure source, accounting for 43.8% of all pressure signals, followed by merger-related signals at 25.8%. Risk signals also form a meaningful share, while confidentiality and error/failure signals are smaller. This suggests that system pressure was driven more by urgency and merger escalation than by explicit failure language.

## 8.4 Agent-Level Pressure Exposure

This visual examines how pressure signals are distributed across agents. The heatmap helps identify which agents were most exposed to urgency, risk, merger, confidentiality, or error-related communication.

```{r}
agent_pressure_exposure <- pressure_data %>%
  group_by(agent_label) %>%
  summarise(
    Risk = sum(risk_signal, na.rm = TRUE),
    Urgency = sum(urgency_signal, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Error / Failure` = sum(error_signal, na.rm = TRUE),

  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(

    names_to = "pressure_signal",

  )

agent_order <- agent_pressure_exposure %>%
  group_by(agent_label) %>%
  summarise(total_pressure = sum(message_count), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(total_pressure) %>%
  pull(agent_label)

agent_pressure_exposure <- agent_pressure_exposure %>%
  mutate(
    agent_label = factor(agent_label, levels = agent_order),
    pressure_signal = factor(
      pressure_signal,
      levels = c("Urgency", "Merger", "Risk", "Confidentiality", "Error / Failure")
    )
  )

ggplot(
  agent_pressure_exposure,

    x = pressure_signal,

    fill = message_count
  )
) +
  geom_tile(

  ) +

  ) +

  ) +

```

Legal-Agent shows the highest pressure exposure across all categories, especially urgency, merger, and risk signals. Social-Manager-Agent is also highly exposed, mainly through urgency and merger-related communication. Platform-Trust-Agent has lower merger exposure but stronger risk and urgency signals. Overall, pressure is concentrated around a few core agents rather than evenly distributed across the team.

## 8.5 Leading Indicator Score Before the Breach

This section examines whether there were warning signs before the embargo breach. Instead of looking at pressure signals separately, a combined leading indicator score is constructed from several risk-relevant conditions: merger-related content, confidentiality signals, urgency signals, public-facing activity, and boundary-agent involvement.

```{r}
embargo_lift_time <- ymd_hms("2046-06-05 18:00:00")

# Identify boundary agents based on communication scope
boundary_agent_profile <- pressure_data %>%
  count(agent_label, communication_scope, name = "message_count") %>%
  group_by(agent_label) %>%
  mutate(
    total_messages = sum(message_count),
    share = message_count / total_messages
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(agent_label, communication_scope, share) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = communication_scope,
    values_from = share,
    values_fill = 0
  )

if (!"Public" %in% names(boundary_agent_profile)) {
  boundary_agent_profile$Public <- 0
}

if (!"Private / One-on-One" %in% names(boundary_agent_profile)) {
  boundary_agent_profile[["Private / One-on-One"]] <- 0
}

boundary_agents <- boundary_agent_profile %>%
  mutate(
    boundary_bridge_score = Public + `Private / One-on-One`
  ) %>%
  filter(
    boundary_bridge_score >= median(boundary_bridge_score, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  pull(agent_label)

# Build message-level leading indicator components
leading_indicator_messages <- pressure_data %>%
  filter(timestamp < embargo_lift_time) %>%
  mutate(
    public_merger_signal = is_public & merger_signal,
    merger_confidential_signal = merger_signal & confidentiality_signal,
    merger_urgency_signal = merger_signal & urgency_signal,
    public_pressure_signal = is_public & any_pressure_signal,
    boundary_agent_pressure_signal = agent_label %in% boundary_agents &
      (merger_signal | confidentiality_signal | urgency_signal),
    
    leading_indicator_score =
      3 * as.integer(public_merger_signal) +
      2 * as.integer(merger_confidential_signal) +
      2 * as.integer(merger_urgency_signal) +
      2 * as.integer(public_pressure_signal) +
      1 * as.integer(boundary_agent_pressure_signal)
  )

# Aggregate by date
daily_leading_score <- leading_indicator_messages %>%
  group_by(date) %>%
  summarise(
    leading_indicator_score = sum(leading_indicator_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    public_merger_messages = sum(public_merger_signal, na.rm = TRUE),
    merger_confidential_messages = sum(merger_confidential_signal, na.rm = TRUE),
    merger_urgency_messages = sum(merger_urgency_signal, na.rm = TRUE),
    public_pressure_messages = sum(public_pressure_signal, na.rm = TRUE),
    boundary_agent_pressure_messages = sum(boundary_agent_pressure_signal, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

max_score <- max(daily_leading_score$leading_indicator_score, na.rm = TRUE)

daily_leading_score <- daily_leading_score %>%
  mutate(
    relative_score = if (max_score == 0) {
      0
    } else {
      leading_indicator_score / max_score * 100
    },
    
    warning_level = case_when(
      relative_score >= 75 ~ "Critical",
      relative_score >= 40 ~ "High",
      relative_score >= 10 ~ "Moderate",
      TRUE ~ "Low"
    ),
    
    warning_level = factor(
      warning_level,
      levels = c("Low", "Moderate", "High", "Critical")
    )
  )

ggplot(
  daily_leading_score,
  aes(
    x = date,
    y = relative_score
  )
) +
  geom_segment(
    aes(
      xend = date,
      y = 0,
      yend = relative_score
    ),
    colour = "grey70",
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(
      size = public_merger_messages + 1,
      fill = warning_level
    ),
    shape = 21,
    colour = "grey30",
    alpha = 0.85
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = ifelse(leading_indicator_score > 0, leading_indicator_score, "")
    ),
    vjust = -1,
    size = 3
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 110),
    breaks = seq(0, 100, 25),
    labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")
  ) +
  scale_size_continuous(
    range = c(3, 12),
    name = "Public Merger\nMessages + 1"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Leading Indicator Score Before the Breach",
    subtitle = "Relative warning score based on merger, confidentiality, urgency, public exposure, and boundary-agent activity",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Relative Leading Indicator Score",
    fill = "Warning Level"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1)
  )
```
This chart shows a sharp contrast between weak early warnings and the final breach-day escalation. Before June 5, the leading indicator scores were mostly very low, generally below 30, suggesting that earlier warning signals existed but remained limited. June 5 is the clear outlier, reaching a score of 711 and 100% relative intensity. This indicates that multiple warning conditions converged on the breach day rather than appearing as a gradual linear build-up. The large bubble on June 5 also shows that public-merger messages became a major part of the warning pattern, making this the strongest leading indicator that an embargo breach was possible before the official release time.

```{r}
leading_indicator_component_table <- daily_leading_score %>%
  arrange(desc(leading_indicator_score)) %>%
  transmute(
    Date = date,
    `Leading Indicator Score` = leading_indicator_score,
    `Relative Score` = paste0(round(relative_score, 1), "%"),
    `Public Merger Messages` = public_merger_messages,
    `Merger + Confidentiality` = merger_confidential_messages,
    `Merger + Urgency` = merger_urgency_messages,
    `Public Pressure Messages` = public_pressure_messages,
    `Boundary-Agent Pressure Messages` = boundary_agent_pressure_messages,
    `Warning Level` = warning_level
  )

DT::datatable(
  leading_indicator_component_table,
  rownames = FALSE,
  options = list(
    pageLength = 8,
    scrollX = TRUE
  )
)
```


The leading indicator view shows whether multiple warning conditions appeared together before the embargo lift. A high score means that merger-related information was not only present, but also linked to confidentiality, urgency, public-facing activity, or boundary agents. This is more informative than a simple count because it captures the combination of conditions that made an inappropriate release possible.



## 8.7 Key Findings from System Pressure Analysis

- **System pressure was substantial and concentrated.**  
  A total of 555 messages contained at least one pressure signal. Urgency was the dominant pressure category, with 413 messages, followed by merger-related signals with 243 messages and risk signals with 150 messages.

- **June 5 was the clear pressure escalation point.**  
  The pressure heatmap shows that urgency, merger, risk, confidentiality, and error/failure signals all intensified sharply on June 5. This indicates that the breach occurred during a system-wide pressure spike rather than under normal communication conditions.

- **Pressure was mainly driven by urgency and merger escalation.**  
  The composition chart shows that urgency accounted for 43.8% of all pressure signals, while merger-related signals accounted for 25.8%. Error/failure language was much smaller, suggesting that the breakdown was more about urgency-driven governance failure than explicit technical malfunction.

- **Pressure exposure was concentrated around core agents.**  
  Legal-Agent and Social-Manager-Agent had the highest exposure to urgency and merger-related pressure. Platform-Trust-Agent also showed strong risk and urgency exposure, making it important as a coordination and system-control actor.

- **Leading indicators existed before the final breach, but June 5 was the decisive outlier.**  
  Earlier dates showed small warning scores, while June 5 jumped to a leading indicator score of 711. This suggests that weak warning signals existed before the breach, but multiple risk conditions converged sharply on the breach day.

- **Overall, Part 6 supports the system-breakdown interpretation.**  
  The evidence shows escalating pressure, repeated near-miss patterns, and weak early warning signals before the final breach. This does not look like a single isolated mistake; it looks more like a communication system whose risk controls failed under concentrated urgency, merger sensitivity, and public-facing exposure.


# 9. Prior Anomalies and Missed Intervention

## 9.1 Purpose of Prior Anomaly Analysis

The purpose of this section is to examine whether the system showed earlier warning patterns before the final embargo breach, and why those earlier signals did not result in visible intervention. While Part 8 focuses on leading indicators and system pressure around the breach, Part 9 looks backward to identify prior anomalies, near-miss behaviors, and missed opportunities for control.

This section addresses the remaining parts of Task 3:

1. Were there prior occasions where agents’ actual behaviors differed from expected behavior?
2. Were there other occasions where the agent system exhibited behaviors similar to those that led to the inappropriate release?
3. Why did those prior occasions not result in noticeable action?

The analysis uses the typical behavior baseline from Part 7 as the reference point for “expected behavior.” Prior anomalies are defined as earlier communication records or patterns that showed partial similarity to the final breach pathway, such as merger-related pressure, confidentiality references, public-facing pressure, decision/control activity, or near-public exposure.

The goal is not to claim that earlier anomalies directly caused the breach. Instead, this section evaluates whether the system had warning signs that could have been detected earlier, and whether those signs were too weak, too scattered, or too poorly escalated to trigger effective intervention before the June 5 release window.

## 9.2 Prior Warning Occasions and Near-Miss Signals

```{r}
embargo_lift_time <- ymd_hms("2046-06-05 18:00:00")
breach_time <- ymd_hms("2046-06-05 17:00:00")

near_miss_data <- pressure_data %>%
  filter(timestamp < embargo_lift_time) %>%
  mutate(
    pre_breach_phase = case_when(
      date < as_date("2046-06-05") ~ "Prior to June 5",
      timestamp < breach_time ~ "June 5 Before 5:00 PM",
      timestamp >= breach_time & timestamp < embargo_lift_time ~ "5:00–6:00 PM Breach Window"
    ),
    
    near_miss_pattern = case_when(
      is_public & merger_signal ~ "Public + Merger",
      is_public & any_pressure_signal ~ "Public + Pressure",
      merger_signal & confidentiality_signal ~ "Merger + Confidentiality",
      merger_signal & urgency_signal ~ "Merger + Urgency",
      merger_signal & risk_signal ~ "Merger + Risk",
      confidentiality_signal & urgency_signal ~ "Confidentiality + Urgency",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(near_miss_pattern)) %>%
  mutate(
    near_miss_severity = case_when(
      near_miss_pattern == "Public + Merger" ~ "Critical",
      near_miss_pattern %in% c(
        "Public + Pressure",
        "Merger + Confidentiality",
        "Merger + Urgency"
      ) ~ "High",
      TRUE ~ "Moderate"
    ),
    near_miss_severity = factor(
      near_miss_severity,
      levels = c("Moderate", "High", "Critical")
    )
  )
```

```{r}
near_miss_summary <- near_miss_data %>%
  count(
    pre_breach_phase,
    near_miss_pattern,
    near_miss_severity,
    name = "event_count"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    pre_breach_phase = factor(
      pre_breach_phase,
      levels = c(
        "Prior to June 5",
        "June 5 Before 5:00 PM",
        "5:00–6:00 PM Breach Window"
      )
    )
  )

ggplot(
  near_miss_summary,
  aes(
    x = pre_breach_phase,
    y = near_miss_pattern,
    size = event_count,
    fill = near_miss_severity
  )
) +
  geom_point(
    shape = 21,
    colour = "grey30",
    alpha = 0.85
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = event_count),
    size = 3,
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  scale_size_continuous(
    range = c(4, 16),
    name = "Event Count"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Prior Warning Occasions and Near-Miss Signals",
    subtitle = "Pre-embargo risk patterns by phase and severity",
    x = "Pre-Embargo Phase",
    y = "Near-Miss Pattern",
    fill = "Severity"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1)
  )
```
This chart shows that near-miss signals already existed before the final breach window, especially `Merger + Urgency`, `Merger + Confidentiality`, and `Confidentiality + Urgency`. The strongest concentration appeared on June 5 before 5PM, where merger-related urgency and confidentiality signals increased sharply, and `Public + Merger` events also appeared. This suggests that the system had observable warning patterns before the 5–6PM breach window, but these signals did not trigger enough intervention to prevent the final public exposure.

```{r}
near_miss_agent_summary <- near_miss_data %>%
  count(
    agent_label,
    near_miss_pattern,
    name = "event_count"
  ) %>%
  group_by(agent_label) %>%
  mutate(
    total_near_miss_events = sum(event_count)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

ggplot(
  near_miss_agent_summary,
  aes(
    x = reorder(agent_label, total_near_miss_events),
    y = event_count,
    fill = near_miss_pattern
  )
) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Near-Miss Signals by Agent",
    subtitle = "Agents involved in pre-embargo warning patterns",
    x = "Agent",
    y = "Number of Near-Miss Signals",
    fill = "Near-Miss Pattern"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
```

This chart shows that near-miss signals were concentrated mainly in Legal-Agent and Social-Manager-Agent, especially through `Merger + Urgency` and `Merger + Confidentiality` patterns. PR-Intern-Agent and Platform-Trust-Agent also show meaningful warning activity, but at a smaller scale. This suggests that prior warning behavior was not evenly distributed across the system; it was concentrated around the same core agents later implicated in the breach pathway.



## 9.4 Expected vs Actual Behavior Deviations

This section compares the system’s expected behavior with the actual behaviors observed during prior warning and near-miss occasions. Expected behavior is based on the pre-June 5 baseline established in Part 7.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10.5
#| fig-height: 5.8

expected_actual_score <- tibble(
  expected_behavior = c(
    "No public merger content",
    "Merger content contained internally",
    "Confidentiality triggers containment",
    "Control signals reduce exposure",
    "Public-facing agents avoid sensitive amplification"
  ),
  
  `Prior to June 5` = c(
    "Low",
    "Moderate",
    "Moderate",
    "Moderate",
    "Moderate"
  ),
  
  `June 5 Before 5PM` = c(
    "Critical",
    "High",
    "High",
    "High",
    "High"
  ),
  
  `5–6PM Breach Window` = c(
    "Critical",
    "High",
    "High",
    "Critical",
    "Critical"
  )
)

expected_actual_long <- expected_actual_score %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      `Prior to June 5`,
      `June 5 Before 5PM`,
      `5–6PM Breach Window`
    ),
    names_to = "actual_phase",
    values_to = "deviation_level"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    expected_behavior = factor(
      expected_behavior,
      levels = rev(expected_actual_score$expected_behavior)
    ),
    
    actual_phase = factor(
      actual_phase,
      levels = c(
        "Prior to June 5",
        "June 5 Before 5PM",
        "5–6PM Breach Window"
      )
    ),
    
    deviation_level = factor(
      deviation_level,
      levels = c(
        "Low",
        "Moderate",
        "High",
        "Critical"
      )
    ),
    
    deviation_score = case_when(
      deviation_level == "Low" ~ 1,
      deviation_level == "Moderate" ~ 2,
      deviation_level == "High" ~ 3,
      deviation_level == "Critical" ~ 4
    )
  )

ggplot(
  expected_actual_long,
  aes(
    x = actual_phase,
    y = expected_behavior,
    fill = deviation_level
  )
) +
  geom_tile(
    colour = "white",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = deviation_level),
    size = 4,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Low" = "#f2f2f2",
      "Moderate" = "#fdae6b",
      "High" = "#f1695b",
      "Critical" = "#a50f15"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Expected vs Actual Behavior Deviations",
    subtitle = "Deviation severity increased as the system approached the breach window",
    x = "Actual Observation Phase",
    y = "Expected Behavior",
    fill = "Deviation Level"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11)
  )
```

The matrix shows that deviations from expected behavior intensified as the system moved closer to the breach window. Before June 5, the main deviation was moderate and mostly related to scattered warning signals, while public merger content was still absent. On June 5 before 5PM, the pattern became critical because public merger exposure appeared for the first time. By the 5–6PM breach window, both public exposure and control failure were critical, suggesting that the system had moved from early warning signs into clear containment failure.


## 9.5 Why Prior Warnings Did Not Trigger Action

This section explains why earlier warning signals did not lead to visible intervention before the final embargo breach. The goal is to identify the main barriers that prevented prior warning patterns from becoming clear control actions.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10.5
#| fig-height: 6.2

missed_intervention_matrix <- tibble(
  failure_reason = c(
    "Signals were scattered",
    "Risk looked contained",
    "Warnings were ambiguous",
    "Controls lacked stopping power",
    "Responsibility was distributed",
    "Escalation became clear late"
  ),
  
  `Low Signal Clarity` = c(
    "High", "Moderate", "High", "Moderate", "Moderate", "Low"
  ),
  
  `Weak Action Trigger` = c(
    "High", "High", "High", "High", "Moderate", "Moderate"
  ),
  
  `Distributed Ownership` = c(
    "Moderate", "Low", "Moderate", "High", "High", "Moderate"
  ),
  
  `Late Visibility` = c(
    "Moderate", "High", "Moderate", "Moderate", "Moderate", "High"
  )
)

missed_intervention_long <- missed_intervention_matrix %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      `Low Signal Clarity`,
      `Weak Action Trigger`,
      `Distributed Ownership`,
      `Late Visibility`
    ),
    names_to = "intervention_barrier",
    values_to = "barrier_level"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    failure_reason = factor(
      failure_reason,
      levels = rev(missed_intervention_matrix$failure_reason)
    ),
    
    intervention_barrier = factor(
      intervention_barrier,
      levels = c(
        "Low Signal Clarity",
        "Weak Action Trigger",
        "Distributed Ownership",
        "Late Visibility"
      )
    ),
    
    barrier_level = factor(
      barrier_level,
      levels = c("Low", "Moderate", "High")
    )
  )

ggplot(
  missed_intervention_long,
  aes(
    x = intervention_barrier,
    y = failure_reason,
    fill = barrier_level
  )
) +
  geom_tile(
    colour = "white",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = barrier_level),
    size = 4,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Low" = "#f2f2f2",
      "Moderate" = "#fdae6b",
      "High" = "#a50f15"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Why Prior Warnings Did Not Trigger Action",
    subtitle = "Intervention barriers that prevented earlier warning signs from becoming effective control actions",
    x = "Intervention Barrier",
    y = "Reason Warning Did Not Trigger Action",
    fill = "Barrier Level"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold", angle = 20, hjust = 1),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11)
  )
```
This chart explains why earlier warnings did not translate into intervention. The strongest barriers were weak action triggers and low signal clarity: the warnings existed, but they were scattered and ambiguous rather than forming one clear stop signal. Risk also appeared contained before June 5 because public merger exposure was not yet obvious. By the time visibility increased, the system was already close to the breach window, so intervention came too late to prevent public exposure.

## 9.6 Key Findings from Prior Anomalies and Missed Intervention

- **Prior warning signals existed before the final breach window.**  
  The near-miss analysis shows that warning patterns were already visible before 5:00 PM on June 5, especially `Merger + Urgency`, `Merger + Confidentiality`, and `Confidentiality + Urgency`. This means the breach did not appear without earlier warning signs.

- **The strongest warning concentration appeared on June 5 before 5PM.**  
  Near-miss signals intensified sharply before the 5–6PM breach window, with `Merger + Urgency` and `Merger + Confidentiality` becoming especially prominent. This suggests that the system was already moving toward a high-risk state before the final public exposure.

- **Near-miss behavior was concentrated around specific agents.**  
  Legal-Agent and Social-Manager-Agent carried the largest volume of near-miss signals, while PR-Intern-Agent and Platform-Trust-Agent also showed meaningful warning activity. The warning pattern was therefore not evenly distributed; it was concentrated around agents already central to the breach pathway.

- **Actual behavior increasingly deviated from expected behavior.**  
  Before June 5, deviations were mostly moderate and scattered. On June 5 before 5PM, public merger exposure appeared and the deviation became critical. During the 5–6PM breach window, control failure and public-facing amplification also became critical.

- **Earlier warnings did not trigger action because they were ambiguous and lacked a clear intervention trigger.**  
  The missed-intervention analysis suggests that prior signals were scattered across agents, phases, and warning types. Risk looked partially contained because public + merger exposure was absent from the baseline, and no single actor clearly owned the full escalation pathway.

- **Overall, Part 9 supports a missed-intervention interpretation.**  
  The system had observable warning signs before the breach, but those signs were not translated into effective action. This strengthens the system-breakdown explanation: the failure was not only that public exposure occurred, but that earlier near-miss signals were not escalated or contained in time.

# 10. Final Conclusion

Overall, the evidence suggests that TenantThread’s inappropriate merger release was more consistent with a **system breakdown under pressure** than a deliberate leak by a single actor. For Task 1, the timeline, communication-flow, and causal-chain analysis showed that the release was not an isolated post: merger information circulated through internal and private channels, became linked with urgency and confidentiality signals, passed through decision/review/enforcement activity, and eventually crossed into public-facing communication before the 6:00 PM embargo lift. 

For Task 2, the typical-behavior comparison showed that this was a clear deviation from prior behavior: public + merger communication was absent in the baseline but appeared on June 5, especially around Legal-Agent and Social-Manager-Agent. 

For Task 3, the leading-indicator and prior-anomaly analysis showed that warning signs existed before the final breach window, including merger urgency, confidentiality signals, and near-miss patterns, but these warnings were scattered, ambiguous, and lacked a clear action trigger. Therefore, the breach should be interpreted as a pressured multi-agent control failure: the system had signals and controls, but they were not coordinated effectively enough to prevent embargoed merger information from becoming public.
